candidates.exact_span: Alternative 8 - The percent solids of sewage sludge that contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 90% based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a 90% percent-solids numeric limit; different readings of what counts as percent solids, the moisture/total-solids basis, or the 'prior to mixing' timing could change which limit applies or whether a reported measurement exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or an anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines whether Alternative 8's 90% limit is applicable at all; interpreting aerobic/anaerobic treatment status or what constitutes unstabilized solids could change whether a numeric limit comparison is required.

candidates.exact_span: When cover is placed on an active surface disposal site, the methane gas concentration in the air in any structure shall not exceed 25% of the lower ex plosive limit (LEL) for methane gas during the period that the disposal site is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a 25%-of-LEL numeric methane limit conditioned on cover placement and site-active status; interpreting when cover is placed, what structures are covered, or when the site is 'active' could change limit applicability, linked continuous-monitoring obligations, and how missing methane data is classified.

candidates.exact_span: The concentration of methane gas in air at the property line of the surface disposal site shall not exceed the LEL for methane gas during the period that the disposal site is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a property-line methane limit at 100% LEL (distinct from the 25%-LEL structure limit); interpreting LEL measurement basis or when the disposal site is 'active' could change numeric compliance comparisons, continuous-monitoring requirements, and missing-evidence handling.

candidates.exact_span: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) Test - Once/Permit Life, performed within one year from the effective date of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines a permit-life TCLP monitoring obligation with a one-year post-effective-date window; different readings of permit effective date or what satisfies 'Once/Permit Life' could change whether monitoring was required and whether absent TCLP results represent a documented no-data state versus missing required evidence.

Establishes annual PCB monitoring frequency; interpreting the monitoring period or whether PCB monitoring applies could change obligation applicability and classification of periods without PCB results.

candidates.exact_span: Methane Gas in covered structures on site - Continuous
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires continuous methane monitoring in covered on-site structures; interpreting which structures are 'covered' or what 'Continuous' requires could change monitoring obligations and how gaps in methane data are treated.

candidates.exact_span: Methane Gas at property line - Continuous
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires continuous property-line methane monitoring; interpreting the property-line location or continuous-monitoring standard could change obligation applicability and missing-evidence semantics for absent readings.

candidates.exact_span: All other pollutants shall be monitored at the frequency shown below:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scopes which pollutants fall under the sludge-amount-based frequency table versus the explicitly listed parameters; different interpretations of 'all other pollutants' could change which monitoring requirements apply and which missing results are in scope.

candidates.exact_span: Amount of sewage sludge* (metric tons per   365 day period)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The sludge-amount metric (including the footnoted asterisk and 365-day rolling basis) determines monitoring tier; interpreting how sludge amount is calculated or what the asterisk denotes could change required frequency and expectations when results are absent.

Sets annual monitoring for lower sludge-amount tiers; boundary interpretation at 0 and 290 metric tons could change which frequency applies and thus whether missing data reflects a required monitoring period.

Sets quarterly monitoring for mid-tier sludge amounts; boundary interpretation at 290 and 1,500 metric tons could change required monitoring frequency and missing-evidence classification for unaudited quarters.
